batchName: Empire: Roman Art and Architecture (c. 500 BC-AD 476) - Medium Batch 2
chapterName: Empire: Roman Art and Architecture (c. 500 BC-AD 476)

questions.question: By the 3rd century AD, where did most of the water from Rome's aqueducts go?
questions.explanation: By then Rome had eleven aqueducts supporting over a million people. The baths consumed most of their flow.
questions.sourceQuote: By the 3rd century AD the city had eleven, supporting over a million people, and most of the water went to the public baths.

questions.question: Which combination did Roman temples typically follow?
options: A Greek layout with steps on every side
An Etruscan layout with Greek column styles
An Egyptian layout with Greek columns
A Greek layout with Etruscan columns
An Etruscan layout with no columns at all
questions.explanation: Temples sat on a high platform with steps only at the front, but used Doric, Ionic or Corinthian columns. The main room, the cella, housed the god's statue.
questions.sourceQuote: Temples followed an Etruscan layout, with a high platform and steps only at the front, but used Greek column styles: the plain Doric, the scroll-topped Ionic and the leafy Corinthian.

questions.question: Which of these building types were Roman inventions? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The amphitheatre, basilica and triumphal arch were among the few building types Romans invented. The arch was borrowed from the Etruscans and the Doric column from the Greeks.
questions.sourceQuote: The amphitheatre, an oval arena ringed by tiered seats, was one of the few building types the Romans invented, along with the basilica and the triumphal arch (*arcus triumphalis*).

questions.question: What does the famous statue group of the Tetrarchs, now in Venice, depict?
questions.explanation: Carved around AD 305, the Tetrarchs show the blocky late Roman style. The same look appears on the Arch of Constantine.
questions.sourceQuote: A famous statue group of four co-ruling emperors, the Tetrarchs, carved around AD 305 and now in Venice, shows the same blocky look.

questions.question: Once concrete walls carried the weight of a building, what role did columns often play?
options: They held up the roof alone
They channelled water through their cores
questions.explanation: Columns had once been essential supports. With load-bearing concrete walls, they often became decorative.
questions.sourceQuote: Columns, once essential supports, often became mere decoration in front of load-bearing walls.

questions.question: What did Pliny the Elder complain had happened to true portrait painting?
options: It had become too costly to commission
It had been replaced by mosaics
It had been banned by the emperor
It had been ruined by Greek slaves
It had died out through laziness
questions.explanation: Pliny's encyclopedia is the main ancient source on Roman art. He grumbled that the craft of true portrait painting had faded.
questions.sourceQuote: Pliny the Elder, the 1st-century AD writer whose encyclopedia is our main ancient source on art, grumbled that true portrait painting had died out through laziness.

questions.question: In the Fayum region of Roman Egypt, what were realistic painted portraits attached to?
questions.explanation: These rare panel portraits survive from a farming region of Roman Egypt. They are a precious exception, since most panel painting has rotted away.
questions.sourceQuote: Rare panel portraits survive from the Fayum, a farming region of Roman Egypt, where realistic painted faces were attached to mummies.

questions.question: Under Augustus, quarries at which place in northern Italy were opened to supply marble to the capital?
questions.explanation: Carrara marble began flowing to Rome from Augustus's reign. Fine coloured marbles were also imported from Greece.
questions.sourceQuote: But from his reign the quarries at Carrara in northern Italy were opened up for the capital, and fine coloured marbles were imported from Greece.

questions.question: What were the imagines carried at the funerals of great Roman families?
questions.explanation: Masks of ancestors were worn in funeral processions. None of them survives, but many surviving busts probably depict such ancestors.
questions.sourceQuote: Ancestral busts were displayed in the entrance hall (*atrium*) of an aristocratic house, and at the funerals of great families, masks of the forebears (*imagines*) were worn in procession.

questions.question: After Christianity took hold, who were the only subjects of big statues?
questions.explanation: Christianity ended large religious statues, so only emperors got colossal figures. Giant fragments of a colossal Constantine survive.
questions.sourceQuote: Christianity soon ended large religious statues; big figures were made only of emperors, like a colossal Constantine whose giant fragments survive.
